title: Recomp guide (part. 3): performance & body fat loss/distribution
summary: In the last part of his recomp guide he says gym performance is the gauge of a working recomp: strength and tonnage should rise at constant bodyweight. Training should stay progression-focused with high intensity rather than cut-style high volume. From his own recomp he describes uneven, uncontrollable fat loss, mostly visceral, with arms and legs keeping or gaining size.
claims: Gym performance is a measure of a recomp: at the same bodyweight, trading fat for muscle should make you stronger
Fat adds some strength as a spring and because mass moves mass, but muscle adds far more because moving is its only purpose
Getting weaker on a recomp means you are either losing weight because you did not track, or losing muscle because of hormones, unsuitable diet or training
On a working recomp tonnage rises; feeling depleted or quitting partway through workouts means it is failing and you must reassess
His strength has gone up since starting the recomp; some main lifts stall but variations and accessories keep progressing
Unlike a cut, a recomp should not hurt training; if you are losing strength you are no longer recomping
Do not change your training when you start a recomp; keep programming for progression, accept slower gains than on a bulk and occasionally retaking a day
Do not panic and modify the program when a day does not progress; it destroys your ability to judge whether the recomp works
He responds to very high volume with high intensity and needs a lot of tonnage to grow; others may need less
Do not fall for the high-volume fallacy of cuts: lowering intensity and adding volume just means low-intensity work, since volume and intensity exist together
On a recomp train with the highest possible intensity, varied so you hit different rep ranges, and increase volume over time
Spot reduction exists in that fat comes off some areas first, but you cannot control it; fat-loss creams and pills are marketing
On his recomp his legs lost no fat and even grew at the same bodyweight, while his abs, obliques, shoulders and traps got much leaner; his chest always holds fat
Fat loss is uneven and seems to follow an order; his face leaned out quickly and then stalled
A proper recomp makes the body shed visceral fat while keeping subcutaneous and intramuscular fat it needs for performance under heavy training
His arms kept their size and even grew, triceps especially, still measuring 17.5 inches while looking leaner with biceps veins
Gaining muscle makes an area look leaner, so visual fat-loss judgments on a recomp are tricky
A recomp lets you get both size and shreds; the catch is that it is very slow and requires commitment
Already-lean areas like forearms and feet do not lose fat; the body prioritises fattier spots
Muscle built on the biceps can be fuelled by fat taken from elsewhere, like the love handles, so a growing body part need not shrink
Training abs with nucleus overload does not spot-reduce them; the body may even send more fat around a trained muscle, but it looks leaner because the muscle grows
